facts.fact: The Zambia Cyber Security Agency said creating, altering or sharing misleading AI-generated audio, video and images may be an offence under Section 19 of the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025, with a fine up to K280,000 and 2 to 7 years in prison.

ZMB.note: Document states nothing on government use of AI.
Document states nothing on AI in a sector's public system.
Document states nothing on AI built or hosted in the country.

facts.fact: The Zambia Cyber Security Agency (ZCSA) acts as the national agency under the Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025, issuing a public advisory on online misuse.
ZCSA issued a public advisory warning of rising social media misuse, including scams, false information and deepfakes, and urging verification before sharing.
ZCSA cited Sections 19 and 22 of the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025, which carry fines and prison terms for deceptive or false electronic communications, as law that can be prosecuted now.

ZMB.note: No dated arrest, charge or conviction is stated, so no use of the law.
A warning of penalties under a law on false content, with no one reported charged and no cut stated.
